conclusions: Four new parameter cases in two already-known families were fully evaluated in separately owned paired sessions from identical shared live first proposals. Both arms accepted zero of four first or repaired solutions.

The legacy arm admitted three of four public formulations; bounded generation admitted four. The sole rejected legacy formulation returned zero equations for three required outputs. Structural admission does not establish formula correctness or beneficial use.

All twenty physical Super calls delivered complete JSON with known usage, no retry, provider failure, truncation, syntax, certificate-schema, output-contract or authorization failure. Mathematical failures were reached, not inferred from unexecuted tests.

Fifteen of sixteen allocated certificates were numerically wrong as written. One later treatment certificate was mathematically equivalent across its outputs but one value was noncanonical, so unchanged exact acceptance rejected it. That is distinct from a numerically wrong certificate; no retroactive regrading or answer normalization occurred.
Twenty-four allocated calls / 61234 tokens include four shared-prefix replays. Actual physical usage was twenty calls / 50216 tokens; 11018 common-prefix tokens are explicitly charged twice.

Each arm used twelve calls. Treatment used 32442 tokens versus 28792 legacy, about 12.68 percent more. Two pairs met the predeclared five-percent whole-stage and repair-only tolerance; treatment used no more compute in only one pair. The predeclared formulation, functional and repair signals remain false.

Frozen outcome counts, reference confidentiality, exact oracle, default Ultra and authority remain unchanged. The temporary push launcher is removed; no additional experiment is dispatched by this receipt.
